description: REVALIDATED 2026-08-17. Previously blocked on 'identify and recruit a specific external non-maintainer contributor and authorize the contact channel', which stalled the entire submission-path validation behind finding a willing outside person. That dependency is not real. Everything this item actually verifies - that the documented flow works, that CI validation fires correctly on a fork PR, and that the trust checks distinguish a fork from a maintainer mirror - is reproducible from a maintainer-owned secondary account with no write access to the repo. The fork-vs-maintainer trust logic in .github/workflows/validate-submission.yml keys on head.repo.fork and author_association, both of which a secondary-account fork exercises exactly as an outsider's would. Recruiting a genuine outsider is still worth doing later for unbiased friction data, but it is a research nicety and must not gate the engineering validation. The one thing a self-owned fork cannot prove is whether the docs are followable by someone without project context; mitigate by following the written steps literally and recording every deviation.

anti_patterns.dont: bundle defect fixes into this TODO
anti_patterns.why: mixing observation with implementation muddies the retrospective; file separate TODOs and keep this one focused on the dry-run experience.

anti_patterns.dont: interpret a frictionless human dry-run as evidence the human run was unnecessary
anti_patterns.instead: frictionless from a human is success of the prep, not redundancy of the test, and confirms the docs are now where they need to be.
anti_patterns.why: the agent-proxy run on 2026-04-28 already pre-fixed obvious friction via the dry-run-followup-* TODOs

anti_patterns.dont: pre-coach the contributor through the docs
anti_patterns.why: that hides the friction this dry-run exists to surface.

anti_patterns.dont: skip the external recruit and use another maintainer
anti_patterns.why: every maintainer already shares the curse of knowledge.

preserves.behavior: Phase 2's trust-label distinction - community submissions retain `community-submission`, never silently promoted.

The contributor's autonomy - no real-time hand-holding during the dry-run.

work_units.notes:
Criteria:
  - Familiar with running CLI tools and opening GitHub PRs
  - Has access to a SQL platform supported by BenchBox (DuckDB at minimum)
  - Willing to submit a real benchmark result and write a few
    sentences of feedback afterwards
  - Not currently working on BenchBox internals
Reach out via the channel where target users live (data community
Slack/Discord, Twitter, direct ask to a known data engineer). One
contributor is enough for this iteration.
work_units.summary: Create or use a maintainer-owned secondary GitHub account, fork the repo, and confirm it has no write access

work_units.notes:
Send the contributor:
  1. The link to `docs/contributing-results.md` (and only that link -
     do not coach them through the steps).
  2. The repo URL.
  3. A one-paragraph "what we'd love feedback on" note (not a script;
     just the framing).
Critical: do NOT walk them through the steps in real time. Let them
hit the docs cold. The friction points only surface if you don't
smooth them.
work_units.summary: From the fork, follow docs/contributing-results.md verbatim with no insider knowledge and no local shortcuts

work_units.notes:
Ask the contributor to keep notes on:
  - Steps they had to re-read or guess at
  - Errors they hit and how they resolved them
  - Tools/dependencies they didn't already have
  - Anything in the docs that turned out to be wrong/missing
Intervene only if blocked for >30 minutes. Capture the timeline:
when they started, when CI ran, when the PR landed.
work_units.summary: Record every point of friction encountered while following the documented path

work_units.notes:
The PR should:
  - Trigger validate-submission CI cleanly
  - Carry a community-submission trust label after merge
  - Render correctly in the explorer after redeploy
Resolve any defects in this PR review like a normal review (don't
skip the rigour because they're external; that defeats the test).
Capture the PR URL/number, merge timestamp, base branch, and final
trust label in the retrospective; verification must query GitHub for
these facts rather than inferring success from local git history.
work_units.summary: Open the fork PR against published-results, let CI validate it, and merge it if valid

work_units.notes:
For each friction item, decide:
  - Doc fix (short edit to contributing-results.md → in-line in this
    TODO)
  - Tool/CLI fix (defect → file separate TODO with steps to reproduce)
  - Process gap (e.g., "no review SLA mentioned" → file under the
    Phase 2 ops runbook TODO)
Write a short human-specific retrospective at
`_project/handoffs/external-human-dry-run-retrospective-<date>.md`
summarizing what worked, what didn't, and the resulting TODO list.
Include a compact evidence block with:
  - `human_dry_run: true`
  - `contributor_type: external`
  - `github_pr: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/<n>`
  - `base_branch: published-results`
  - `merged_at: <ISO timestamp>`
  - `trust_label: community-submission`
  - `s28_fork_comment_verified: true | blocked-on-#993`   # see w6
The existing 2026-04-28 and 2026-04-29 agent-proxy retrospectives are
useful prior evidence but must not satisfy this TODO's verification.
work_units.summary: Convert friction notes to follow-up TODOs

work_units.notes:
The dry-run PR is (by design) a FORK PR to published-results — the only way
to exercise the §2.8 fork-PR comment fix against reality. Every
maintainer/mirror PR is same-repo, and the repo has 0 forks today, so §2.8
was implemented (PRs #1000 develop + #1001 published-results) but NEVER
verified end-to-end. This unit closes that gap using w4's real external
fork PR.

HARD PRECONDITION: only meaningful once the repo default_branch is
`develop` (PR #993 + the manual default switch in
docs/operations/branch-rename-runbook.md). A `workflow_run` companion fires
only from the DEFAULT branch, so validate-submission-comment.yml does not
run until develop is the default. If the dry-run runs before that switch,
record w6 as blocked-on-#993 in the retrospective, do not mark it done.

Observe and record in the retrospective evidence block:
  - The fork PR's `Validate Submission` check is GREEN when the bundle
    validates (the read-only-token 403 on the inline "Post PR comment
    (same-repo fast path)" step did NOT redden it — continue-on-error held).
  - The `Submission Validation Comment` workflow_run companion ran and the
    comment (marker `## Submission Validation`) is present, posted by
    github-actions[bot], with NO duplicate.
  - `s28_fork_comment_verified: true | blocked-on-#993`
If the companion did not post but the artifact uploaded, capture the
workflow_run logs URL for follow-up debugging.
work_units.summary: Verify the section 2.8 fork-PR validation-comment path fires on the real fork PR
